text:
Juuse Saros is having the kind of start that makes last season look like the outlier. A year ago he finished 10.2 goals below expected over 59 games. Through 15 starts this season he has saved 9.3 goals above expected, meaning he has kept out 9.3 more goals than the shots he faced would usually allow, 83rd percentile among goalies. His .917 save rate is solid, and his record (7-4-4) undersells how well he has played. By our wins-added measure, his saves rank fourth among 76 goalies.

The best stretch came in early November: a shutout in Los Angeles on Nov. 10 for his first of the season and Nashville's fifth straight win, on the night the club celebrated Pekka Rinne, capping what The Tennessean called a "busy couple of days." He is above league average on low-, medium- and high-danger shots alike, which is a better sign than one hot band. Sunday in San Jose was a rare off night (four goals, below expected). Nashville has had three goalies on the ice at practice, but he has made all 15 of his appearances as the starter.
